Date: 2027-02-20
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jenna Morales (Nova - Head Partnerships), Tom Ruiz (Nova Sales Lead), Priya Anand (Nova Solutions Architect)
Recorded: yes
summary: Weekly co-sell pipeline review. Reviewed top three joint opportunities, alignment on next plays for Acme and Zenith, and planned technical benchmark for a high-value account. Agreed to share co-sell deck, populate joint pipeline, and run a benchmarking session to validate latency/cost on Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted. Discussed security questions (SOC 2, SSO, KMS) and comp structure for referral/intro. Next steps assigned.
topics:
1) Pipeline review: Acme (P0), Zenith (P0/P1), Meridian (P2)
2) Technical validation plan for Acme (latency/cost/quant)
3) Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency)
4) Co-sell GTM and compensation model
5) Next steps and owners
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see the Nova crew. Quick check on agenda - pipeline review, a couple of technical asks from Acme, and then GTM / comp.
[00:18] Jenna Morales (Nova): Yeah thanks Alice, excited. We have a few accounts heating up. Jenna here, I can run through the top opps first.
[00:30] Tom Ruiz (Nova): Quick note, schedule wise both Acme and Zenith want vendor calls in the next two weeks.
[00:40] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Great, Marcus from Redwood here. For the Acme ask, I saw the notes about wanting <5 00 ms tail latency for chat and tight cost constraints, we'll probably need to validate on Dedicated with kv cache and batching - but we can run a quick hosted baseline too.
[01:05] Priya Anand (Nova SA): Acme is particularly sensitive about data residency and audit logs; they asked about KMS and SOC 2 evidence, also SSO for admin.
[01:20] Alice Chen: Yep totally. We'll share our security pack - SOC 2 report, SAML/SSO docs, KMS integration notes and an audit log example.
[01:30] Jenna: For comp, how do you normally structure partner referral/introductions?
[01:40] Alice: We have a few models - referral fee on closed ARR, or joint AE credit and motion-based splits. I'll send the partner compensation outline after this call.
[01:50] Tom: Sounds good. Back to pipeline - Acme is roughly $1.2M ARR potential, champion is Sarah K, procurement timeline end of Q2. Zenith is about $450k, earlier stage. Meridian is exploratory.
[02:10] Marcus: For Acme's latency target, do you have sequence lengths or expected concurrency?
[02:20] Priya: Their use case is multi-turn support assistant, average prompt 250 tokens, peak concurrency ~30.
[02:30] Marcus: That maps - we'll propose a Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity to hit tail latencies, and we can run a hosted baseline to measure unit cost. Our benchmark plan will include 99th percentile latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1,000 tokens.
[02:50] Jenna: Good, can you also throw in quantization guidance? They asked about smaller model footprint to reduce cost.
[03:00] Marcus: Yep, we'll include recommendations: 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs, model variants that keep quality, and an eval plan.
[03:12] Alice: Let's walk the pipeline spreadsheet - Jenna, did you populate the sheet from last week?
[03:20] Jenna: I added Acme and Zenith rows but need to fill expected close dates and champion emails, will do after this call.
[03:28] Alice: Please add ARR, stage, next step and whether they'd consider Dedicated vs Hosted. That helps prioritize.
[03:36] Tom: For Acme, champion is okay with a short pilot but procurement needs contract language for data handling. Any standard terms?
[03:44] Alice: We have a partner-friendly MSA and a one-page DPA. I'll attach the legal package. For private deployments they can do a VPC option but that adds lead time.
[03:56] Priya: They asked specifically about HSM/KMS key management; can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[04:04] Marcus: Yes, we support customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private; for hosted we support envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise. We'll include KMS notes in the security pack.
[04:20] Jenna: Good. On GTM - do you have joint marketing assets or a battlecard for partner AEs to use?
[04:28] Alice: We have a co-sell deck and a short battlecard that outlines value props, competitor positioning, and pricing pointers. I'll share them.
[04:36] Tom: Competitors - Acme asked about comparisons to Anthropic and OpenAI for safety and cost. Any quick talking points?
[04:46] Marcus: High level - we focus on production economics: predictable latency, caching, Dedicated capacity and observability. For safety, we point to our evals and quality monitoring, but specific model comparisons depend on the model variant. We'll include a slide with a simple matrix.
[05:04] Alice: Let's surface the top asks per account: Acme needs latency/cost validation + SOC2/KMS; Zenith needs pricing flexibility and a quick pilot; Meridian wants architectural best practices.
[05:20] Jenna: For Zenith they prefer a hosted POC first, they want to avoid long procurement cycles.
[05:28] Alice: That's fine - hosted POC then potentially move to Dedicated if they need throughput.
[05:36] Marcus: One technical note - when we benchmark, we should capture KV cache hit rates and prefix caching assumptions because that affects token cost dramatically.
[05:48] Priya: Acme will use long conversations so kv cache is critical.
[05:52] Marcus: OK we'll design tests with realistic turn lengths and cache warmup patterns.
[06:00] Jenna: Any blockers from your side on booking joint calls with customers?
[06:06] Alice: No blockers. Once Jenna shares intro, we'll propose a two-hour joint workshop: 30 minutes GTM, 90 minutes technical deep dive for Acme.
[06:18] Tom: For dates, they prefer March 8 or 9.
[06:24] Alice: We'll tentatively hold March 9, pending champion availability.
[06:30] Marcus: On BDD (bench) logistics - we'll need access to a small dataset or synthetic prompt template from Acme to mimic their distribution; can Nova collect that?
[06:42] Priya: We can help. I'll work with Sarah's team to get a scrubbed prompt set.
[06:48] Marcus: Great, that will make the numbers meaningful.
[06:52] Jenna: Anything on revenue crediting? If Redwood closes, do Nova gets referral?
[06:58] Alice: We do referral fees or co-sell credit; specifics in the partner comp doc I'll share - usually tied to motion and who drives the opportunity.
[07:10] Tom: Okay makes sense.
[07:14] Alice: Quick check on internal resourcing - Marcus will lead the technical bench, I will lead GTM and account motion, and Jenna/Tom will lead partner intro/outreach.
[07:26] Jenna: Yep.
[07:28] Alice: Any outstanding legal concerns beyond DPA and KMS?
[07:32] Priya: Nothing else right now, procurement might ask about SLAs and uptime for Dedicated.
[07:38] Alice: We have SLA templates for Dedicated customers - I'll include that.
[07:42] Marcus: Also note that Dedicated deployment lead times vary by region; if Acme requires EU data residency we should flag capacity planning early.
[07:54] Jenna: Acme is US-first but might expand to EU next year.
[07:58] Alice: Noted. We'll call that out.
[08:02] Tom: For the benchmarking session, what metrics will you deliver?
[08:08] Marcus: 99th/95th/50th latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens for the workload, model quality delta vs baseline, and recommended config (batching, quantization, cache).
[08:24] Priya: Perfect. Also include a short appendix on fallbacks - model variant fallbacks if capacity constrained.
[08:34] Marcus: Will do.
[08:36] Alice: Anything else on GTM? Joint webinars later this quarter?
[08:40] Jenna: Let's wait until we have a success story from Acme or Zenith, but we can plan a customer webinar in Q3.
[08:48] Alice: Cool. Let's recap next steps.
[08:52] Marcus: I'll draft the benchmark plan and share it by Friday (2027-02-26).
[08:58] Alice: I'll share co-sell deck + comp doc + legal package by Wednesday (2027-02-23). Jenna to intro champions and Tom to update pipeline by Thursday (2027-02-24).
[09:12] Jenna: Sounds good, we'll action those.
[09:16] Tom: One last quick ask - can Redwood provide a short slide comparing cost/latency of hosted vs Dedicated for typical support assistant workload?
[09:26] Marcus: Yes, that's part of the benchmark deliverable; I'll include an illustrative slide.
[09:32] Alice: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in threads and update the shared pipeline doc.
[09:38] Jenna: Thanks all.
[09:40] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[09:42] (call ends)
references: Co-sell deck: https://drive.redwood/example-cosell-deck, Shared pipeline sheet: https://sheets.redwood/joint-pipeline-nova, Security pack (SOC2/DPA): https://redwood.docs/security-pack
